facebook.long_form:
🥎 **AUGUST 5 AT THE #LLSWS — DAY 3 RESULTS + AUSL PRO GAME TONIGHT**

Tuesday's action at Stallings Stadium delivered.

Northwest beat Southwest 7-3 in a loser-bracket elimination game — Madison Locke led the way with 3 hits, 3 runs, and 4 RBI. Mid-Atlantic (Toms River, NJ) mercy-ruled New England (Bristol, CT) 13-3 in four innings. Two more teams went home.

The host team — North Carolina's Johnston County squad, making their first-ever LLSWS appearance — remains undefeated at 2-0. They don't play today.

Tonight is the marquee event: the 2026 AUSL Pro Game at 7 PM ET on ESPN2. Twenty-four of the world's best softball players, split into two teams, coached by softball legends Lisa Fernandez and Natasha Watley. They're playing at the same Stallings Stadium where the LLSWS is unfolding. Players spent Tuesday doing first pitches and meet-and-greets at the LLSWS games, and this morning they hosted a youth Tee Ball clinic for two local Little League programs.

You'll see the kids watch the pros play tonight. That's the whole point.

stories.title: Montana Fouts Won the AUSL and the International Cup — In the Same Two Weeks

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Montana Fouts in July:

✅ Utah Talons win 2026 AUSL Championship (July 26)
✅ Named AUSL Pitcher of the Year (7-4, 2.36 ERA, 63 K)
✅ Pitches USA WNT to International Cup gold over Japan (Aug 3)

Two titles. Three weeks. One pitcher. 🥎

#Softball #USASoftball

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The AUSL All-Star Cup starts August 8 in Rosemont, IL.

45 players. 12 games on ESPN, MLB Network, and CBS Sports Network.

Fouts. Allchin. Brady. Coleman. The best players in the game — all in one place.

Don't sleep on this. 🥎

#AUSL #Softball

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **MONTANA FOUTS' SUMMER: TWO TITLES, THREE WEEKS**

On July 26 in College Station, Texas, the Utah Talons beat the Chicago Bandits 6-1 to win the 2026 AUSL Championship. Montana Fouts pitched. The Talons won back-to-back AUSL titles. Jadelyn Allchin was the MVP — she homered, doubled, drove in three runs, and made a headfirst diving catch that became the defining highlight of the postseason.

Fouts was also named AUSL Pitcher of the Year: 7-4, 2.36 ERA, 63 strikeouts in 61.1 innings. Her strikeout-to-walk ratio was 63:10. Opponents hit .200 against her. She set multiple AUSL single-season records.

Three weeks later, she was back in Oklahoma City at Devon Park — but this time for the USA Women's National Team. She took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of the International Cup gold medal game and beat No. 1 Japan 2-0.

Back-to-back AUSL titles. International Cup gold. Named to the All-Star Cup roster.

The AUSL All-Star Cup starts August 8 in Rosemont, Illinois. Twelve games on ESPN, MLB Network, and CBS Sports Network through August 30. Don't miss it.

---

stories.title: Texas Tech's Transfer Class Goes Deeper — Kasidi Pickering Is a 50-HR Outfielder

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Texas Tech's transfer class also includes Kasidi Pickering (OU).

Career: .384 BA, 50 HR, 169 RBI. 2026: .370/20 HR/61 RBI.

2024 national champion. WCWS All-Tournament.

This class is different. 🥎

#Softball #SoftballRecruiting

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **TEXAS TECH'S TRANSFER CLASS GOES DEEPER THAN BEACHUM**

Everyone heard about Jaysoni Beachum committing to Texas Tech — and for good reason. .406 average, 10 HR, 69 RBI at FSU, 2024 NFCA Freshman of the Year.

But the deeper you look at the TTU transfer class, the more impressive it gets.

Kasidi Pickering came from Oklahoma. Three seasons as a Sooner: .384 career average, 50 home runs, 169 RBI across 186 games. In 2026 alone she hit .370 with 20 home runs and 61 RBI in 59 games. She was part of the 2024 national championship team at OU and made the WCWS All-Tournament Team. She has one season of eligibility remaining.

Then there's Jayden Heavener — a pitcher from LSU who went 13-9 with a 2.81 ERA in 2026 and has two years of eligibility left. Pitching depth has been the one thing standing between Texas Tech and the national title conversation. Heavener fills that gap.

Beachum + Pickering + Heavener. Add those to what was already an elite roster.

This isn't just the No. 1 transfer class. This is a team built to win in 2027.

---

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **SEPTEMBER 1 IS 27 DAYS AWAY — THE FILM IS DONE**

The summer showcase season is over. PGF Nationals, major tournaments, the Little League Softball World Series — everything that matters for the Class of 2028 has happened. The evaluation window is closed.

Right now, Division I coaches are reviewing every clip, every game log, every at-bat from the summer circuit. They're building the list of who they call first on September 1 — the day they can pick up the phone and dial a Class of 2028 recruit directly for the first time.

For prospects who had a big summer: the calls are coming. The question is which programs are calling, and in what order.

For prospects who underperformed at their biggest showcases: there's still time. September showcases exist. Coaches adjust. But the window to make a first impression on September 1 is being decided right now.

27 days. The phones will ring. Make sure you were the one worth calling.

stories.title: Philippines "Blu Girls" Are Chasing Their First Asian Games Softball Medal Since 1998

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
The Philippines "Blu Girls" haven't won an Asian Games softball medal since 1998.

That's 2014, 2018, and 2022 all ending in 4th place.

In July they stunned No. 3 Puerto Rico 5-4 on a walk-off in Lima.

Sept 26. Aichi-Nagoya. They're coming for a medal. 🥎

#Softball #AsianGames

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **THE PHILIPPINES "BLU GIRLS" ARE GOING TO AICHI-NAGOYA FOR A MEDAL**

The Philippines national softball team — known as the Blu Girls — haven't medaled at the Asian Games since 1998. Three consecutive Games ended in 4th place: 2014, 2018, 2022. Close each time. No medal.

They're ranked No. 13 in the world and 4th in Asia. Japan (host, World No. 1) enters as the overwhelming favorite. But something happened in Lima, Peru last month that changed the conversation.

At the WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Group Lima qualifier, the Philippines faced Puerto Rico — the No. 3 team in the world. Walk-off win for the Blu Girls, 5-4. They stayed alive in the qualifier. They showed up when it counted.

September 26. Aichi-Nagoya. The Asian Games softball competition begins. The Philippines will be there, and this time they're not just hoping to medal.

They're training for it.

---
